_rules.note: Every Character sets their Role's Role Ability to Rank 4 at creation, in all three methods.

rockerboy.name: Rockerboy
rockerboy.tagline: Street poets with a mic and a grudge, weaponizing art against the powerful.
rockerboy.flavorText: You live to rock, and in Night City that makes you dangerous. Rockerboys are the street poets and loudmouths, the ones who put the truth to a beat and shove it in the face of everyone with power. You do not need a label or a stadium. A porta-studio, the Data Pool, and a message nobody wants to hear will do fine. Johnny Silverhand did it with a guitar and a grudge, and the Corps are still nervous. Some nights you play a dive in the Combat Zone for beer money. Some nights you turn a crowd into a mob. You can make the timid brave and the comfortable afraid. Use it while you can. After all, you came to play.

roleAbility.name: Charismatic Impact
roleAbility.summary: The Rockerboy's Role Ability is Charismatic Impact. With this ability, they can influence others by sheer presence of personality. They need not be a musical performer; they can influence others through poetry, art, dance, or simply their physical presence. They could be a rocker, or a cult leader. As they grow in skill, they can affect larger and larger groups and call on their fans for greater and greater requests of loyalty.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Rockerboy's Role Ability is Charismatic Impact. They can influence others by sheer presence of personality: through music, poetry, art, dance, or simply their physical presence. They could be a rocker, or a cult leader. A Rockerboy can only use Charismatic Impact on Fans. Outside of combat you can turn non-fans into fans (unless they actively dislike you) by rolling Charismatic Impact + 1d10 vs. DV8 for a single person, DV10 for a Small Group of up to 6, or DV12 for a Huge Group. The GM decides when someone you meet is already a Fan. When you ask a favor of a fan or group, the GM checks the favor against your current Rank. If it's beyond your Rank you automatically fail. Otherwise group size sets the DV and you roll Charismatic Impact + 1d10. On a success the fans give their best effort; on a failure you can't ask that same favor of those fans again for a week. Each Rank sets the best venue you can play and what you can ask of a single fan (DV8), a small group of up to 6 (DV10), and a huge group (DV12): Ranks 1–2: Venues: small local clubs. Single: a small favor (buy you a drink/meal, give you a lift). Small Group: fans ask for autographs and stop you in the street. Huge Group: none yet.
Ranks 3–4: Venues: well-known clubs. Single: a major favor (put in a good word, etc.). Small Group: regularly hang out and supply party favors. Huge Group: a strong local following that buys your recordings and merch.
Ranks 5–6: Venues: large, important clubs. Single: commit a minor crime (shoplift, help in a fight). Small Group: act as your personal posse. Huge Group: loyal fans across the City doing major favors for attention.
Ranks 7–8: Venues: small concert halls, local video feed. Single: risk their life for you without question. Small Group: commit a minor crime for you. Huge Group: rabidly loyal: they fight rival fans and band together to help you.
Rank 9: Venues: large concert halls, national video feed. Single: commit a major crime. Small Group: commit a major crime. Huge Group: a cult-like following that will riot, destroy property, even kill for you.
Rank 10: Venues: huge stadiums or international video. Single: sacrifice themselves for you without question. Small Group: risk their lives as personal protection. Huge Group: a worldwide, cult-like following: effectively a private army built on your charisma.

solo.name: Solo
solo.tagline: Freelance killers and corporate samurai, the deadliest hardware in the Time of the Red.
solo.flavorText: You were born with a gun in your hand, the meat one, before the other arm became a weapons platform. Solos are the muscle of the Time of the Red: freelance killers, bodyguards, corporate samurai gone ronin. Most of you did time in somebody's war, and it shows in the chrome, the reflexes, and the combat drugs you can't quite quit. When you are the best, you name your price, and it is very high. But there is a bill for all of it. You have traded so much flesh for edge that you flinch at your own reflection, and trust is a luxury you cannot afford. One night it's a penthouse, the next it's an alley. That's the job. That's being a Solo.

roleAbility.name: Combat Awareness
roleAbility.summary: The Solo's Role Ability is Combat Awareness. With Combat Awareness, a Solo can call up their training to have an enhanced situational awareness of the battlefield. When combat begins, anytime outside of combat, or in combat with an Action, a Solo may divide the total number of points they have in their Combat Awareness Role Ability among a number of combat abilities. If a Solo chooses to not change their point assignments, their previous ones persist. Activating some of these abilities will cost the Solo more points than others.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
When combat begins (before Initiative is rolled), anytime outside of combat, or in combat with an Action, a Solo may divide the total points they have in their Combat Awareness Role Ability among the abilities below. If they don't change their assignments, the previous ones persist. Some abilities cost more points than others. Damage Deflection: trained to roll with the punches. For 2 points decrease the first damage you take this Round by 1; 4 points by 2; 6 points by 3; 8 points by 4; 10 points by 5.
Fumble Recovery: for 4 points, you ignore critical failures (natural 1s) rolled while attacking. Those rolls still count as a 1.
Initiative Reaction: each point adds +1 to your Initiative rolls.
Precision Attack: for 3 points, +1 to any Attacks; 6 points, +2; 9 points, +3.
Spot Weakness: each point adds +1 to the damage (before armor) of your first successful Attack in a Round.
Threat Detection: each point adds +1 to any Perception Checks.

netrunner.name: Netrunner
netrunner.tagline: Brain-burning cowboys who jack into the New NET and walk out with its secrets.
netrunner.flavorText: You are a brain-burning cowboy of the Post-NET, and you got there the hard way. The old NET died screaming in the 4th Corp War, so you do not lounge on a couch and dream. You move your meat, jack in on-site, and walk architectures full of Black ICE that would love to stop your heart. You started young, cracking school systems and skimming bank accounts, chasing the ghosts of gods like Bartmoss. Now you run with a crew: Solos on your back, a Medtech to restart you, a Tech to soup up your deck. You slip into the hardest systems in the city and walk out with their secrets. The ICE might get you one day. Until then, you ride bare-brained and headfirst.

roleAbility.name: Interface
roleAbility.summary: The Netrunner's Role Ability is Interface. Interface is what allows the Netrunner to Netrun, to interface with electronic mind-modems (called cyberdecks) to control computers, electronics, and associated programming. The Interface Role Ability also gives the Netrunner access to a wide suite of Abilities related to computer hacking and system control.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
A Netrunner's Interface Role Ability lets them Netrun, sets how many NET Actions they take on their Turn, and grants a suite of Interface Abilities. (The full Netrunning rules are covered separately.) NET Actions per Turn by Interface Rank: Rank 1–3 = 2 actions; Rank 4–6 = 3; Rank 7–9 = 4; Rank 10 = 5. Interface Abilities:
Backdoor: break through Passwords and other obstructions in the Architecture.
Cloak: hide your actions in the Architecture before you leave.
Control: control things attached to the Architecture.
Eye-Dee: identify a found piece of data and its value.
Pathfinder: learn the “map” of the Architecture.
Scanner: find the locations of systems in an area.
Slide: slip away from one Black ICE that is following you.
Virus: leave a custom virus at the core of the Architecture.
Zap: a basic Netrunner attack that works against both Programs and other Netrunners.

tech.name: Tech
tech.tagline: Renegade mechanics and mad inventors who keep the Dark Future running.
tech.flavorText: You cannot leave anything alone. If it sits near you too long you have already opened it up and made it into something better. Techs keep the Dark Future running: you build, fix, and modify in a world the War broke and never fully repaired. Everyday jobs pay the rent. The real money is in the work nobody advertises: illegal weapons, hot cybertech, corporate gear for corporate crimes. That trade buys you friends and a longer list of enemies, so you invest in defenses and keep a Solo or two on speed dial. You have patched hardware for black-ops samurai and for the old lady down the block, and nobody comes back to complain. Maybe that's the turrets on your door. Maybe you're just that good.

roleAbility.name: Maker
roleAbility.summary: A Tech can fix, improve, modify, make, and invent items using Maker, their Role Ability. Each time their Maker Rank rises they gain a Rank in two Maker Specialties of their choice: Field Expertise, Upgrade Expertise, Fabrication Expertise, or Invention Expertise.
roleAbility.mechanicalText: A Tech can fix, improve, modify, make, and invent new items using Maker, their Role Ability. Whenever a Tech increases their Maker Rank by 1, they gain 1 Rank in two different Maker Specialties (Field Expertise, Upgrade Expertise, Fabrication Expertise, or Invention Expertise) of their choice. Field Expertise: Add your Rank in this Specialty to any Basic Tech, Cybertech, Electronics/Security Tech, Weaponstech, or Land/Sea/Air Vehicle Tech Skill Check made for a non-Maker purpose. With at least 1 Rank, instead of a lengthy full repair you can jury-rig a target to perfect condition (full SP and HP) as an Action at the item's normal repair DV, adding your Field Expertise Rank. The fix holds 10 minutes per Rank, after which the item reverts and can't be jury-rigged again until fully repaired. Upgrade Expertise: Improve an item in one of the listed ways (an item can benefit from only one such upgrade): e.g. lower non-borgware cyberware Humanity Loss by 1d6 (if normally 2d6+), add a slot, halve future repair time, make a one-handed weapon concealable, raise Average to Excellent quality, add an Attachment Slot or non-basic ammo to an Exotic weapon, +1 SP (if it had any), a Nomad-Rank-1 vehicle upgrade, or install one of your own inventions. Roll TECH + the item's usual repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10; buy materials of the item's price category (consumed). DV and time scale with price category. On a failure you start over, but materials and item are unharmed. Fabrication Expertise: Build an existing or self-invented item from materials. Roll TECH + the item's usual repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10; buy materials one price category below the item (Super Luxury items need materials worth half their Price). DV and time scale with price category; a failure means starting over with materials intact. Invention Expertise: Invent a new item or upgrade. Describe its function to the GM in terms of existing technology; if approved, the GM sets its rules and a Price Category (minimum Expensive). Roll TECH + the relevant repair Skill + this Rank + 1d10. Once invented, it can be built with Fabrication or Upgrade Expertise. The GM may rebalance an invention over time. Upgrade / Fabricate / Invent DV & Time by cost: Cheap/Everyday DV9, 1 hour; Costly DV13, 6 hours; Premium DV17, 1 day; Expensive DV21, 1 week; Very Expensive DV24, 2 weeks; Luxury DV29, 1 month; Super Luxury DV29, 1 month per 10,000eb of Cost.

medtech.name: Medtech
medtech.tagline: Back-alley doctors who keep the crew breathing when they've no right to be.
medtech.flavorText: You keep people alive who have no business being alive. In the Time of the Red a Medtech is half doctor and half mechanic, because half your patients are more chrome than flesh. If you were lucky you trained at one of the med schools still standing in the ruins of the old country. Then the War came, and you learned the rest fast, in the field, with the wrong tools and the clock running. Now you patch bodies mid-firefight, install chrome in back rooms, and decide who is worth the last dose. The crew that has you comes home. The crew that doesn't buries people. You are the difference, and everyone in the room knows it.

roleAbility.name: Medicine
roleAbility.summary: The Medtech's Role Ability is Medicine. With this ability, Medtechs can keep people alive who should be dead with their knowledge, tools, and training. In the Time of the Red, they are as much doctors as they are mechanics, caring for people who are often more machine than human. Whenever the Medtech increases their Medicine Rank, they also choose one of three Medicine Specialties to allocate a single point to: surgery, pharmaceuticals, or cryosystems operation.
roleAbility.mechanicalText: The Medtech Role Ability is Medicine. Whenever the Medtech increases their Medicine Rank, they allocate 1 point to one of three Specialties: Surgery, Medical Tech (Pharmaceuticals), or Medical Tech (Cryosystem Operation). The Medical rules add uses of the Surgery and Medical Tech Skills available only to Medtechs: including cyberware installation and harvesting, bodysculpting, and therapy. Surgery: Each point gives 2 points in the Surgery Skill (max 10). Surgery is the TECH Skill for treating the most severe Critical Injuries and implanting cyberware, available to Medtechs only through this Specialty. Medical Tech (Pharmaceuticals): Each point gives 1 point in the Medical Tech Skill (max 10; max 5 points in this Specialty). Each point also unlocks one pharmaceutical you can synthesize with a DV13 Medical Tech Check (materials wasted on a failure); from 200eb of materials you make doses equal to your Medical Tech Skill in 1 hour. You can't synthesize Street Drugs this way. Drugs: Antibiotic (a naturally healing target heals +2 HP/day for a week; one at a time); Rapidetox (immediately purges a drug, poison, or intoxicant); Speedheal (a non-Mortally-Wounded target heals BODY + WILL HP; once per day); Stim (ignore Seriously Wounded penalties for an hour; once per day); Surge (function without sleep for 24 hours; once per week). Administering a dose takes an Action; an unwilling target can be hit with an Airhypo Melee Attack to dose them instead of dealing damage. Only a Medtech can administer these correctly. Medical Tech (Cryosystem Operation): Each point gives 1 point in the Medical Tech Skill (max 10; max 5 points here). Benefits by points: 1: one Cryopump; 2: Registered Cryotank Technician with 24/7 access to 1 cryotank at a time at any corporate or government facility; 3: one Cryotank installed in a room of your choice; 4: two more Cryotanks (same room) and a Cryopump with 2 charges carrying up to 2 people in stasis; 5: three more Cryotanks and a Cryopump with 3 charges carrying up to 3 people. Your Medical Tech Skill Level equals your Pharmaceuticals points plus your Cryosystem Operation points.

media.name: Media
media.tagline: Reporters and muckrakers who dig up what the Corps paid to bury.
media.flavorText: Somebody has to tell the truth, and somebody is always going to try to stop them. That's the job. Medias are reporters, streamers, and screamsheet muckrakers who chase the story the Corps paid good money to bury. You go where the cameras aren't supposed to, you talk to people who shouldn't talk, and you put it all on every screen in the city. It is dangerous work. Corporations do not sue you, they retire you. But at higher reach you stop being an annoyance and start being a threat, the kind that topples an Exec or moves a law. Guards get replaced. A good story does not. Point it at the right people and you can change the whole city.

roleAbility.name: Credibility
roleAbility.summary: The Media's Role Ability is Credibility. The Media can not only convince an audience of the truth of what they publish but also has a larger audience the more credible they are. Medias also have greater levels of access to sources and information; they are always in the know with their ears to the ground to pick up on rumors and information passively.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Media Role Ability is Credibility. A Media can convince an audience of what they publish, reaches a larger audience the more credible they are, has greater access to sources and information, and passively picks up rumors. Rumors: As long as you aren't entirely off-grid, at least twice per week the GM secretly rolls your Credibility Rank + 1d10; if it beats a DV on the Rumor Table's Passive column, the GM clues you in on the highest rumor you beat. You can also actively hunt rumors with STAT + a relevant Skill (Library Search, Conversation, Interrogation, etc.) + 1d10 vs. the Active DV. Rumor tiers (Passive DV / Active DV): Vague 7/13, Typical 9/15, Substantial 11/17, Detailed 13/21. Publishing Stories or Scoops: Each Rank sets your Access/Sources (who you can reach), Audience (how far a story spreads), Believability (a d10 chance the audience buys it), and Impact (how much real change a story causes). One piece of easily understood verifiable evidence raises the believe chance by 1; more than 4 distinct hard pieces raises it by 2 (these stack). LUCK can never be spent on a Believability Check. You can't publish another story on the exact same topic without new information. Ranks 1–2: local honchos/gang lords; neighborhood audience; 2-in-10 believe; small incremental change.
Ranks 3–4: city gang honchos, minor politicians, Corp Execs; known local contributor; 3-in-10; local bad guys arrested or ousted.
Ranks 5–6: major City players and politicos, local celebrities; Citywide reach; 4-in-10; change across the City, local laws may pass.
Ranks 7–8: local Corp presidents, mayors, City celebrities; Statewide reach; 5-in-10; mid-level corporations or governments may fall, multi-city laws.
Rank 9: divisional Corp heads, State politicos; national reach; 6-in-10; national change, large corporations or governments may be toppled.
Rank 10: world leaders, major Corporation heads, world-famous celebrities; worldwide reach; 7-in-10; global change: Megacorps and governments may fall, international laws established.

exec.name: Exec
exec.tagline: Corporate power made personal, fighting with money and staff instead of a gun.
exec.flavorText: Once the Megacorps owned the world, and you intend to help them own it again, with you somewhere near the top. Execs are corporate power made personal: you build a team, you pull strings, and you fight with money and staff instead of a gun in your own hand. The suit is armor. The Conapt and the Trauma Team coverage are the leash and the reward. Your people do the dirty work, as long as you keep them loyal and paid, and HR keeps the replacements coming when they don't come back. It is a cold way to run, but it works. In this city the ones with the budget win the fight before it starts. You plan to be one of them.

roleAbility.name: Teamwork
roleAbility.summary: The Exec's Role Ability is Teamwork. Just like a real corporate executive, the Exec builds a team whose members help them accomplish their goals, whether legal or not, morale permitting. Team members have a visible job description (like secretary or driver) but also have a covert roles (such as Netrunner, bodyguard, or assassin). Plus they get free housing and nice set of clothes!.
roleAbility.mechanicalText: The Exec Role Ability is Teamwork: the Exec builds a team whose members help accomplish their goals, morale permitting. Signing Bonus (Rank 1): a Businesswear Jacket, Top, Bottom, and Footwear marking them as business elite (can't be resold without raising suspicion). Corporate Housing (Rank 2): access to a Company Corporate Conapt, rent-free while they remain with the Corporation (Lifestyle is still bought separately). Rank 7 improves it to a Beaverville House in the Executive Zone; Rank 10 to a Beaverville McMansion (Executive Zone) or a Luxury Penthouse (Corporate Zone). A new Corporation matches the offer and pays to move their things. Corporate Health Insurance: Rank 6 grants Trauma Team Silver coverage (Corp-paid monthly); Rank 8 upgrades it to Trauma Team Executive. Team Members: Rank 3 grants 1 Team Member; Ranks 5 and 9 add one more each (max 3 at Rank 9). Team Members are built like PCs but don't improve Skills, are controlled by the GM, and can only wear Light Armorjack. The Exec picks each Team Member's class (Bodyguard, Covert Operative, Driver, Netrunner, Technician, etc.); a 1d6 roll sets their STATs and starting Loyalty is 1d6+1. Loyalty: Team Members act based on Loyalty (caps at 10 between sessions; no cap within a session). When given a task, the GM rolls 1d6 under current Loyalty: a failed Save means they may refuse, botch, or turn on the Exec; at 0 or lower they actively betray the Exec, and ending a session below 0 means they leave. Loyalty is built by things like complimenting work (+1), perks worth 200eb+ (+4), backing them against management (+4), a 20% job cut (+6), paid time off (+6), or risking harm for them (+8); it is lost by neglect (-1), berating them (-2), forgetting their contribution or birthday (-4), broken promises (-6), throwing them under the bus (-6), or abandoning them under fire (-8). Losing a Team Member: HR repossesses their gear and sends a replacement next session with new STATs, starting Loyalty 1, and a 200eb hiring fee to the Exec.

lawman.name: Lawman
lawman.tagline: The badge in a city that eats badges, holding a line nobody thanks them for.
lawman.flavorText: Somebody has to hold the line, even when the line is a joke. Lawmen are the badge in a city that chews badges up: patrol officers, corporate security, Psycho Squad, the last thing standing between order and the Combat Zone. When it goes bad you call for backup, and what rolls up depends on your rank and your luck, from four renta-cops to an AV full of C-SWAT. You answer to a boss with an agenda and a budget, and you make the hard calls nobody thanks you for. Half the city thinks you're the enemy. Some days they're right. But you took the job, and out here the job is the only thing keeping it all from burning.

roleAbility.name: Backup
roleAbility.summary: The Lawman's Role Ability is Backup. With this ability, Lawmen can call upon the help of a group of fellow officers, based on the Lawman's Rank and the conditions under which they make the call. This Backup is armed and armored based on their Rank.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Lawman's Role Ability is Backup: they can call on a group of fellow law enforcers based on their Backup Rank and the situation. Backup is armed, armored, and played by the GM. As a Lawman rises in Rank they're promoted or recruited into agencies they can call Backup from. When in danger, as an Action you call for Backup of your Rank or lower, rolling equal to or under your Backup Rank on a d10 to get a response (abuse it and your Boss will fine you or throw you off the force). On a response, roll 1d6 for how many Rounds until they arrive; on a 6 the arriving Backup is one tier higher (at Rank 10, two groups arrive). If nobody responds, you can try again next Turn. Each tier lists Combat Number (a combined STAT+Skill base you add 1d10 to for attack or defense: Backup can't dodge bullets), SP (Body and Head), HP, and MOVE & BODY:
Ranks 1–2: Corporate Security: 4 renta-cops on foot with Heavy Pistols and Kevlar®. Combat 8 / SP 7 / HP 20 / MOVE & BODY 4.
Ranks 3–4: Local Beat Cops: 4 cops in two Compact Groundcars, Heavy Pistols, Kevlar®. Combat 10 / SP 7 / HP 25 / 5.
Ranks 5–7: Sheriff's Department: 2 County Mounties in a High Performance Groundcar with Heavy Pistols and Assault Rifles, Heavy Armorjack. Combat 14 / SP 13 / HP 35 / 4.
Rank 8: Recovery Zone Marshal: 1 lone marshal on a Superbike with a Very Heavy Pistol, Assault Rifle, Grenade Launcher, and Flak Armor. Combat 16 / SP 15 / HP 50 / 6.
Rank 9: C-SWAT: 2 Psycho Squad hitters with Assault Rifles and Rocket Launchers in Metalgear®, arriving by AV-4. Combat 15 / SP 18 / HP 35 / 4.
Rank 10: National Law Enforcement / Interpol / FBI / Netwatch: 2 serious hitters by AV-4 with Very Heavy Pistols and Assault Rifles in Light Armorjack. Combat 14 / SP 11 / HP 35 / 6. They stay after the fight to investigate, and the same pair keeps responding to related calls until the case closes.

fixer.name: Fixer
fixer.tagline: The number everyone saves. Deals, contacts, and the impossible, for a cut.
fixer.flavorText: You figured out early you were never going to be a Corp golden boy or tough enough to run as a Solo. What you had was a knack for knowing what people want and how to get it for them. For a price. Fixers are the deal-makers and information brokers of The Street, the ones who can find the gun, the doc, the buyer, the way out. You keep a web of contacts and clients and you skim a little off every strand. Night Markets appear when you say they do. A good Fixer never touches the merch and never misses their cut. Everybody in Night City has your number saved. Not everybody can afford to call it.

roleAbility.name: Operator
roleAbility.summary: The Fixer's Role Ability is Operator. Fixers know how to get things on the black market and are adept at navigating the complex social customs of The Street, where hundreds of cultures and economic levels collide. Fixers maintain vast webs of contacts and clients who they can reach out to source goods, favors, or information. Fixers can also source desirable resources and make favorable deals.
roleAbility.mechanicalText:
The Fixer's Role Ability is Operator. Fixers know how to get things on the black market and navigate The Street's tangle of cultures and economic levels, maintaining vast webs of contacts and clients. Contacts & Clients: who the Fixer can reach to source goods, favors, or information (still paid for).
Reach: the highest price category the Fixer can always source; at higher Ranks they can gather other Fixers to run a Night Market, briefly making all price categories available.
Haggle: striking a deal. Roll COOL + Trading + your Operator Rank + 1d10 against the other party's COOL + Trading (+ their Operator Rank if a Fixer) + 1d10. On a success you make one deal of your Operator Rank or lower; only one Fixer deal per transaction.
Grease: blending into the many cultures on and off The Street: knowing their language, social codes, and status marks. Ranks 1–2: local honchos/gang lords. Reach: always source Cheap and Everyday items. Haggle: ±10% of market price. Grease: your immediate neighborhood and its gangs.
Ranks 3–4: city gang honchos, minor politicians, Corp Execs. Reach: up to Expensive items. Haggle: buy 5+ of an item, get one free. Grease: one more culture plus a related language at Skill 4.
Ranks 5–6: major City players and politicos, neighborhood celebrities. Reach: once a month, organize a Night Market to source up to Super Luxury. Haggle: negotiate job pay up 20%. Grease: 3 cultures total, each with a related language at Skill 4.
Ranks 7–8: local Corp presidents, mayors, local celebrities. Reach: up to Very Expensive items. Haggle: on a Luxury/Super Luxury item, pay half now and half in a month (miss it and nobody deals again). Grease: 6 cultures total, each with a related language at Skill 4.
Rank 9: divisional Corp heads, State/City-zone politicos. Reach: up to Luxury items; can add a Midnight Market inside a Night Market. Haggle: ±20% of market price. Grease: blend with Corporate and governmental agencies.
Rank 10: world leaders, major Corporation heads, world-famous celebrities. Reach: always source up to Super Luxury. Haggle: double the pay per person on a Dangerous Job. Grease: blend seamlessly with almost any group, even secret societies or exclusive memberships.

nomad.name: Nomad
nomad.tagline: Road families who move the crew and the cargo, and always know the way out.
nomad.flavorText: The Corps drove your family off the land, so the family took to the road and never looked back. Nomads are the pack, the convoy, the reason cargo gets from one end of the ruined map to the other. You grew up in the driver's seat and under the hood, and there is no vehicle you can't coax into moving. Out in the Badlands your family is your law, your bank, and your backup, and you would die before you'd shame them. In the city they call you a bumpkin until they need something moved past the checkpoints. Then your name is the only one that matters. You've got wheels, you've got people, and you always know the way out. That's a Nomad.

roleAbility.name: Moto
roleAbility.summary: The Nomad's Role Ability is Moto. Whenever a Nomad increases their Rank in Moto, they have the option of adding another stock vehicle (with minimum specs) of their Moto Rank or lower to the pool of Family vehicles they have permission to use from the Family Motorpool or to make an upgrade to one of their current vehicles. Thanks to being around vehicles since birth, Nomads are also able to drive any type of vehicle with tremendous skill.
roleAbility.mechanicalText: The Nomad Role Ability is Moto. Nomad Vehicle Familiarity: A Nomad adds their Moto Rank to any Drive Land Vehicle, Pilot Air Vehicle, Pilot Sea Vehicle, Air Vehicle Tech, Land Vehicle Tech, or Sea Vehicle Tech Skill Check. Family Motorpool: Whenever a Nomad's Role Ability Rank rises, they either add a stock vehicle (minimum specs) of their Moto Rank or lower to the vehicles they may use from the Family Motorpool, or upgrade one already-permitted Family Vehicle with a single upgrade of their Moto Rank or lower. A Nomad can have one Family Vehicle out at a time and can call the Family to swap it for another the next morning (if Family is close by). A destroyed Family Vehicle is fully repaired in a week for 500eb; daily repairs like bullet removal are the Nomad's own responsibility. At Rank 10 the Nomad is promoted to Family leadership and may have all their Family Vehicles out at once; further vehicles are bought at market price and upgrades at 1,000eb each. Family Motorpool by Rank: 1–4: Compact Groundcar, Gyrocopter, Jetski, Roadbike; 5–6: Helicopter, High Performance Groundcar, Speedboat; 7–8: AV-4, Cabin Cruiser, Superbike; 9–10: Aerozep, AV-9, Super Groundcar, Yacht.
